nodes.title: OFF
nodes.description: Turns the connected compatible peripheral off when execution arrives.
nodes.purpose: Turns the connected compatible peripheral off when execution arrives.
nodes.example: Delay.Out → OFF.In; Relay Peripheral reference → OFF.Device.

nodes.title: ON
nodes.description: Turns the connected compatible peripheral on when execution arrives.
nodes.purpose: Turns the connected compatible peripheral on when execution arrives.
nodes.example: On Start → ON.In; Relay Peripheral reference → ON.Device.

nodes.title: Set Value
nodes.description: Writes a numeric value to a peripheral that supports Set Value.
nodes.purpose: Writes a numeric value to a peripheral that supports Set Value.
nodes.example: On Start → Set Value.In; Fan reference → Device; Number 50 → Value.

nodes.title: Toggle
nodes.description: Switches the connected compatible peripheral between on and off.
nodes.purpose: Switches the connected compatible peripheral between on and off.
nodes.example: Button Rising Edge → Toggle.In; Relay reference → Toggle.Device.

nodes.title: Equalizer · per source
nodes.description: Applies three per-source EQ bands: 500 Hz, 3 kHz and 6 kHz, each -6 to +6 dB.
nodes.purpose: Applies three per-source EQ bands: 500 Hz, 3 kHz and 6 kHz, each -6 to +6 dB.
nodes.example: File → Equalizer.Source, Low +3 dB → Play.Source. Execution still connects to Play.In.

nodes.title: Audio file / path
nodes.description: Describes a device audio file. Use sd:/ or flash:/ paths; MP3, AAC, WAV, M4A and FLAC are supported.
nodes.purpose: Describes a device audio file. Use sd:/ or flash:/ paths; MP3, AAC, WAV, M4A and FLAC are supported.
nodes.example: Path sd:/media/alert.wav → Play.Source; Rising Edge.Out → Play.In.

nodes.title: Piano melody
nodes.description: Holds one independent melody. Record replaces the previous melody; Play previews it. Mouse/PC keys record notes; select octave and instrument.
nodes.purpose: Holds one independent melody. Record replaces the previous melody; Play previews it. Mouse/PC keys record notes; select octave and instrument.
nodes.example: Melody → DAC Play.Source; Rising Edge → Play.In. DAC supports chords, passive buzzer one note, active buzzer timed beeps.

nodes.title: Pitch
nodes.description: Shifts per-source pitch by -24 to +24 semitones. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.purpose: Shifts per-source pitch by -24 to +24 semitones. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.example: File → Pitch.Source, Semitones 12 → Play.Source.

nodes.title: Speed
nodes.description: Changes per-source playback speed, 0.25–4×. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.purpose: Changes per-source playback speed, 0.25–4×. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.example: File → Speed.Source, Speed 1.25 → Play.Source.

nodes.title: Offline TTS · basic English
nodes.description: Offline English alert speech, up to 256 characters. Speech rate 0.5–1.5, voice pitch 80–220 Hz, intonation 0–1. Lower rate improves clarity; higher intonation varies the voice. This small synthesizer remains robotic. Requires a DAC.
nodes.purpose: Offline English alert speech, up to 256 characters. Speech rate 0.5–1.5, voice pitch 80–220 Hz, intonation 0–1. Lower rate improves clarity; higher intonation varies the voice. This small synthesizer remains robotic. Requires a DAC.
nodes.example: Text "Temperature high" → TTS.Text; Speech → Play.Source; Rising Edge → Play.In.

nodes.title: Volume
nodes.description: Adds per-source volume processing; Volume is 0–100%. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.purpose: Adds per-source volume processing; Volume is 0–100%. It does not trigger playback.
nodes.example: File → Volume.Source, Volume 60 → Play.Source.

nodes.title: AND
nodes.description: Returns True only when both A and B are True.
nodes.purpose: Returns True only when both A and B are True.
nodes.example: Temperature > 30 and Device Enabled → AND → IF.Condition.

nodes.title: NOT
nodes.description: Inverts a Boolean: True becomes False and False becomes True.
nodes.purpose: Inverts a Boolean: True becomes False and False becomes True.
nodes.example: Wi-Fi Connected → NOT → IF.Condition → reconnect action.

nodes.title: OR
nodes.description: Returns True when at least one of A or B is True.
nodes.purpose: Returns True when at least one of A or B is True.
nodes.example: Low battery and Sensor error → OR → Rising Edge → Alert.In.

nodes.title: Event to Boolean
nodes.description: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.purpose: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Event to Value.In; its Value → action value input and Out → action.In.

nodes.title: Event to Integer
nodes.description: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.purpose: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Event to Value.In; its Value → action value input and Out → action.In.

nodes.title: Event to Number
nodes.description: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.purpose: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Event to Value.In; its Value → action value input and Out → action.In.

nodes.title: Event to Text
nodes.description: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.purpose: Value is always available from the configured field. In forwards one execution pulse to Out; it does not convert a pulse into a measurement. Connect Out to the destination action to apply Value.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Event to Value.In; its Value → action value input and Out → action.In.

nodes.title: Alarm Clock
nodes.description: Calendar alarm using UTC/NTP, a manually set clock, or one DS3231 RTC. Choose a specific date or checked weekdays, Monday first. All date/time fields use UTC. Alarm fires once per scheduled occurrence. Clock valid is false until the selected clock is trustworthy. Set clock applies the manual date/time to Manual or RTC only. Rearm clears occurrence history. Pausing/disabling does not replay missed alarms. Manual time is RAM-only; a battery-backed RTC retains time without power.
nodes.purpose: Calendar alarm using UTC/NTP, a manually set clock, or one DS3231 RTC. Choose a specific date or checked weekdays, Monday first. All date/time fields use UTC. Alarm fires once per scheduled occurrence. Clock valid is false until the selected clock is trustworthy. Set clock applies the manual date/time to Manual or RTC only. Rearm clears occurrence history. Pausing/disabling does not replay missed alarms. Manual time is RAM-only; a battery-backed RTC retains time without power.
nodes.example: Alarm → LED.Toggle or GPIO.Toggle. For offline time add Sensor → DS3231 RTC, wire SDA/SCL and power, choose DS3231 RTC and set its clock once from live device Logics. For Manual choose Manual, enter a date/time, then use Set clock or wire an event to Set clock. Date range: 2000–2099.

nodes.title: Between
nodes.description: Returns True when Value is within the Minimum/Maximum range (inclusive).
nodes.purpose: Returns True when Value is within the Minimum/Maximum range (inclusive).
nodes.example: Voltage → Between.Value, Minimum 11.8, Maximum 12.6 → IF.Condition.

nodes.title: Compare
nodes.description: Compares A > B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A > B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator >; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.title: Equal
nodes.description: Compares A == B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A == B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator ==; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.description: Compares A > B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A > B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator >; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.description: Compares A >= B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A >= B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator >=; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.title: IF
nodes.description: Checks a Boolean and routes execution to True or False. A Boolean-driven IF can start a conditional chain in this editor.
nodes.purpose: Checks a Boolean and routes execution to True or False. A Boolean-driven IF can start a conditional chain in this editor.
nodes.example: Compare.Result → IF.Condition; IF.True → Relay ON.In. Use Rising Edge for a one-time threshold crossing.

nodes.description: Compares A < B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A < B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator <; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.description: Compares A <= B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A <= B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator <=; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.title: Not Equal
nodes.description: Compares A != B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.purpose: Compares A != B. Result is a Boolean (True / False), not an execution trigger.
nodes.example: Temperature → A; B 50; operator !=; Result → Rising Edge.Value → Play.In to act once when the result becomes True.

nodes.title: Boolean to Integer
nodes.description: Converts False to integer 0 and True to integer 1.
nodes.purpose: Converts False to integer 0 and True to integer 1.
nodes.example: Source.Value → converter.Input; converter.Value → a matching typed input.

nodes.title: Boolean to Number
nodes.description: Converts False to 0 and True to 1. This is a data conversion, not an execution event.
nodes.purpose: Converts False to 0 and True to 1. This is a data conversion, not an execution event.
nodes.example: Source.Value → converter.Input; converter.Value → a matching typed input.

nodes.title: Measurement to Number
nodes.description: Converts a numeric measurement unchanged, or False/True to 0/1.
nodes.purpose: Converts a numeric measurement unchanged, or False/True to 0/1.
nodes.example: Source.Value → converter.Input; converter.Value → a matching typed input.

nodes.title: Number to Integer
nodes.description: Truncates toward zero. Values outside the signed 32-bit integer range are unavailable.
nodes.purpose: Truncates toward zero. Values outside the signed 32-bit integer range are unavailable.
nodes.example: Source.Value → converter.Input; converter.Value → a matching typed input.

nodes.title: Text to Number
nodes.description: Parses a complete finite decimal number. Invalid or empty text is unavailable, not zero.
nodes.purpose: Parses a complete finite decimal number. Invalid or empty text is unavailable, not zero.
nodes.example: Source.Value → converter.Input; converter.Value → a matching typed input.

nodes.title: On Change
nodes.description: Produces an execution pulse whenever a Boolean changes, in either direction.
nodes.purpose: Produces an execution pulse whenever a Boolean changes, in either direction.
nodes.example: Compare.Result → On Change.Value → Play.In. This fires on both True and False transitions.

nodes.title: Falling Edge
nodes.description: Produces an execution pulse when a Boolean changes from True to False.
nodes.purpose: Produces an execution pulse when a Boolean changes from True to False.
nodes.example: Device Enabled → Falling Edge.Value → Stop.In.

nodes.title: Rising Edge
nodes.description: Produces an execution pulse when a Boolean changes from False to True. The first available reading establishes a baseline; already True at startup does not fire.
nodes.purpose: Produces an execution pulse when a Boolean changes from False to True. The first available reading establishes a baseline; already True at startup does not fire.
nodes.example: Temperature → Compare > 50 → Rising Edge.Value; Rising Edge.Out → Play.In.

nodes.title: On Start
nodes.description: Produces an execution pulse once when the logic runtime starts.
nodes.purpose: Produces an execution pulse once when the logic runtime starts.
nodes.example: On Start → Play.In; File → Play.Source.

nodes.title: On Wake
nodes.description: Fires once after deep-sleep boot or successful light-sleep return, not cold boot. Wake cause uses the ESP-IDF enum: timer 4, GPIO 7, EXT0 2. Global/group modes still apply.
nodes.purpose: Fires once after deep-sleep boot or successful light-sleep return, not cold boot. Wake cause uses the ESP-IDF enum: timer 4, GPIO 7, EXT0 2. Global/group modes still apply.
nodes.example: On Wake.Out -> LED.Toggle or measurement action.

nodes.title: Branch
nodes.description: On each execution pulse, checks Condition and chooses the True or False path.
nodes.purpose: On each execution pulse, checks Condition and chooses the True or False path.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Branch.In; Compare.Result → Condition; True → Fan ON; False → Fan OFF.

nodes.title: Gate
nodes.description: Passes an incoming execution pulse only while Enabled is True.
nodes.purpose: Passes an incoming execution pulse only while Enabled is True.
nodes.example: Timer.Out → Gate.In; Device Enabled → Gate.Enabled; Gate.Out → Play.In.

nodes.title: Sequence
nodes.description: Routes an execution pulse through First, then Second, in order.
nodes.purpose: Routes an execution pulse through First, then Second, in order.
nodes.example: On Start → Sequence.In; First → Relay ON; Second → Play.

nodes.title: CAN · Configure
nodes.description: One controller per ESP. Starts in listen-only mode at 500 kbit/s. Select the bus bitrate; disable listen-only to transmit or acknowledge frames. Reconfiguration clears queued frames.
nodes.purpose: Configures the MCP2551/TWAI bus at 125, 250, 500 or 1000 kbit/s. Starts listen-only. Disable Listen only to transmit and acknowledge. Reconfiguration clears queues; correct wiring before recovering bus-off.
nodes.example: On Start -> Configure.In; set Listen only false, then Configure.Out -> Send.In. MCP2551 requires 5 V power and a 5 V to 3.3 V level shifter on CRX.

nodes.title: CAN · Received
nodes.description: Event for the latest received frame; -1 accepts all identifiers. Fast bursts can coalesce between Logics ticks. Status reports hardware queue overruns.
nodes.purpose: Receives the latest frame with optional decimal identifier filter (-1 means any). Exposes flags, length and hex Data. Fast bursts can coalesce between Logics ticks; this is not a lossless recorder.
nodes.example: Received.Out -> MQTT Publish.In; Received.Data -> Publish.Text.

nodes.title: CAN · Send
nodes.description: Queues a classic CAN frame without waiting. Identifier is decimal; Data is 0–8 hexadecimal bytes separated by spaces. Remote frames use Length (0–8) and empty Data. Queued is not a delivery acknowledgement.
nodes.purpose: Queues one classic CAN frame. Decimal identifier, optional extended/remote flags, 0-8 space-separated hex bytes. Remote frames use Length and empty Data. Queued does not mean delivered. Transmissions make one attempt.
nodes.example: Timer -> Send.In; identifier 256, data 01 02 FF. Monitor Status.TX failed for missing acknowledgement.

nodes.title: CAN · Status
nodes.description: Controller state and cumulative driver counters. Bus-off requires Configure to restart after correcting wiring, bitrate and termination.
nodes.purpose: Reports controller readiness, bus-off and driver RX-missed/TX-failed counters. Counters reset on Configure. A missing peer or wrong bitrate can cause transmit failures.
nodes.example: Bus off -> Rising edge -> an alarm. Repair wiring/bitrate before using Configure to restart.

nodes.title: GPIO
nodes.description: Select an unused board GPIO. Ports follow the pin capabilities and selected input/output mode. Analog reads use ADC1 while Wi-Fi is active. PWM supports two independent channels.
nodes.purpose: Select an available GPIO and its mode: digital input, pull-up/down input, digital output, PWM, or analog read. Unsupported connectors are disabled. ADC1 remains usable with Wi-Fi. PWM uses up to two independent timers at 100-20000 Hz.
nodes.example: On Start.Out -> GPIO.Set level (High/Low) in Output mode; GPIO.Digital read -> Rising Edge.Value; Number.Value -> GPIO.Duty % and Timer.Out -> GPIO.Write PWM.

nodes.title: Built-in LED
nodes.description: Controls the configured status LED or the board’s built-in LED. Automatic status returns ownership to network indicators. Brightness controls regular LEDs through PWM; RGB color controls require NeoPixel/RGB hardware.
nodes.purpose: Controls the configured status LED or the board built-in LED. ON, OFF, Toggle and Set color take execution pulses. Brightness uses PWM for a regular LED and intensity scaling for NeoPixel/RGB LEDs. RGB color controls require NeoPixel/RGB hardware. Automatic status restores the network indicator.
nodes.example: On Start.Out -> Built-in LED.ON; Timer.Out -> Toggle; a shutdown event -> Automatic status.

nodes.title: Modbus RTU · Read
nodes.description: Queues one read (functions 1-4). Out means queued, not completed. Use Received and Last value for replies; Busy prevents overlapping requests. Addresses are zero based.
nodes.purpose: Queues a nonblocking MS1285 Modbus RTU read. Unit IDs 1-247, functions 1-4, zero-based address and count 1-32. Queued fires before the reply. Busy rejects overlapping requests. Serial settings are shared with the LCD/web monitor.
nodes.example: On Start -> Read.In. Received.Out -> an action; Last read value.Value -> its numeric input. Use a timer plus Status.Busy to poll without overlapping requests.

nodes.title: Modbus RTU · Received
nodes.description: One event for the latest CRC-valid received frame. Unit filter 0 accepts any unit. The bounded monitor also displays invalid frames. Fast bursts may be coalesced between Logics ticks.
nodes.purpose: Fires for a new CRC-valid received frame. Unit filter 0 accepts all units; 1-247 limits it. Hex includes the complete captured frame up to the monitor limit. Rapid bursts can coalesce between Logics ticks. Invalid CRC frames appear in the monitor but do not trigger this event.
nodes.example: Received.Out -> MQTT Publish.In and Received.Hex -> MQTT Publish.Text. Set an exact MQTT topic.

nodes.title: Modbus RTU · Status
nodes.description: Serial transaction busy state and last result or timeout message.
nodes.purpose: Reports whether a read is queued or waiting and the last result, exception or timeout. These signals use the same state as the web and LCD RS485 controls.
nodes.example: Status.Busy -> NOT -> Gate.Enabled; Timer.Out -> Gate.In -> Read.In.

nodes.title: Modbus RTU · Last read value
nodes.description: Unsigned register or coil at index 0-31 in the latest successful read. Value is unavailable during a new request or after an error; test Available before use.
nodes.purpose: Unsigned register/coil value at index 0-31 in the last successful read. Available is false while reading or after an error; an unavailable value is not zero.
nodes.example: Received.Out -> IF.In, Available -> IF.Condition, IF.True -> Plot.In and Value -> Plot.Value.

nodes.title: Sleep
nodes.description: Light sleep resumes RAM; Deep sleep restarts the device. Enable Wake timer (0.001-604800 seconds) and/or connect Wake GPIO. Awake fires only after light sleep. Rejected reports failure. CPU/web/software events cannot run during sleep. Audio/updates or busy storage reject sleep; recordings drain first. Motors stop before entry; external loads are not powered off.
nodes.purpose: Light sleep resumes RAM; Deep sleep restarts the device. Enable Wake timer (0.001-604800 seconds) and/or connect Wake GPIO. Awake fires only after light sleep. Rejected reports failure. CPU/web/software events cannot run during sleep. Audio/updates or busy storage reject sleep; recordings drain first. Motors stop before entry; external loads are not powered off.
nodes.example: Event -> Sleep.In; Wake GPIO.Source -> Sleep.Wake source; On Wake -> LED.Toggle. Release wake level before sleep. Deep sleep needs On Wake, not Awake. Avoid immediate boot-to-sleep loops.

nodes.title: Wake GPIO
nodes.description: Hardware High/Low wake source. Deep sleep requires RTC-capable pins: ESP32 RTC pins, S3 GPIO0-21, C3 GPIO0-5, intersected with board availability and existing assignments. External pull resistor required. Software edges/conditions cannot wake a sleeping CPU.
nodes.purpose: Hardware High/Low wake source. Deep sleep requires RTC-capable pins: ESP32 RTC pins, S3 GPIO0-21, C3 GPIO0-5, intersected with board availability and existing assignments. External pull resistor required. Software edges/conditions cannot wake a sleeping CPU.
nodes.example: Button/sensor interrupt -> selected GPIO; Source -> Sleep.Wake source. RTC alarm outputs may be wired here, but the software Alarm Clock does not run during sleep.

nodes.title: Transfer to Plotter
nodes.description: Sample a numeric or Boolean (0/1) value every 5 seconds, or at a connected Sampling Interval. The Plotter requests queued samples over USB serial or Wi-Fi/IP; the device never streams them continuously. Matching plot names overlay named series in different colors. Optional Sample now execution is limited to the same cadence.
nodes.purpose: Requests the named board action when execution arrives; Requested means submitted, not completed. Sample a numeric or Boolean (0/1) value every 5 seconds, or at a connected Sampling Interval. The Plotter requests queued samples over USB serial or Wi-Fi/IP; the device never streams them continuously. Matching plot names overlay named series in different colors. Optional Sample now execution is limited to the same cadence.
nodes.example: On Start.Out → Connect.In; On connected.Out → a follow-up action.In.

nodes.title: Save Data
nodes.description: Record numeric or Boolean samples every 5 seconds by default. Insert Sampling Interval between source and Value to change cadence. An optional Save sample trigger requests a sample, limited to that cadence; without a trigger, recording is automatic while Logics runs. Records go to configured external SD/SDMMC storage as plain ASCII JSON Lines. Path is a folder, defaults to root, and missing folders are created. Use the same plot/series names as Transfer to Plotter. Requires synchronized device date/time. Queued means accepted by the bounded background writer; the Plotter reports storage errors.

nodes.title: Sampling Interval
nodes.description: Connect a source through Sampling Interval to Save Data.Value or Transfer to Plotter.Value. Set the sample cadence in milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days (1 ms to 365 days). This controls collection; the Plotter requests buffered data separately.
nodes.purpose: Sets the cadence for Save Data and Transfer to Plotter. Accepts numeric or Boolean data. Duration units are milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days; range 1 ms to 365 days. This controls sampling, while the Plotter requests buffered samples on demand.
nodes.example: Source.Value → Sampling Interval.Value; Sampling Interval.Value → Save Data.Value or Transfer to Plotter.Value. Without this node, both use 5 seconds.

nodes.title: Cooldown
nodes.description: Allows a trigger, then suppresses additional triggers during the Seconds cooldown.
nodes.purpose: Allows a trigger, then suppresses additional triggers during the Seconds cooldown.
nodes.example: Alarm event → Cooldown.In, Seconds 30 → Play.In.

nodes.title: Countdown Timer
nodes.description: One-shot countdown, default 5 seconds. Start restarts the full duration. Reset restarts an active countdown or restores an idle timer. Stop cancels without Finished. Remaining (s) shows live time and can feed Plot/Save Data; Running is Boolean. Group Pause preserves time. Duration is captured at Start/Reset.
nodes.purpose: One-shot countdown, default 5 seconds. Start restarts the full duration. Reset restarts an active countdown or restores an idle timer. Stop cancels without Finished. nodes.example: On Start.Out → Countdown Timer.Start; Finished → Built-in LED.Toggle or GPIO.Toggle. Connect another event to Reset or Stop. Range: 0.001–86400 seconds.

nodes.title: Debounce
nodes.description: Waits for a quiet period of Seconds after incoming triggers, filtering rapid repeated input.
nodes.purpose: Waits for a quiet period of Seconds after incoming triggers, filtering rapid repeated input.
nodes.example: Button Rising Edge → Debounce.In, Seconds 0.05 → Toggle.In.

nodes.title: Delay

nodes.title: Repeat
nodes.description: Emits Count total execution pulses: the first immediately, then every Seconds. New triggers during the active repeat are ignored.
nodes.purpose: Emits Count total execution pulses: the first immediately, then every Seconds. New triggers during the active repeat are ignored.
nodes.example: On Start → Repeat.In, Count 3, Seconds 1 → Play.In.

nodes.title: Timer
